jobs.title: Global Public Policy Manager, Compute, Infrastructure & Sovereign AI

reading.body:
Three open AI policy and governance roles are listed, two in Europe and one remote in the United States, and one of them names compute and infrastructure directly in its title.

The pattern is small but pointed. The Cohere role is a public policy job scoped to compute, infrastructure, and sovereign AI, which places policy work inside the physical buildout rather than beside it. The other two are a consulting position in Munich and a reporting job at Newsweek, so the category spans advisory and media as well as corporate government affairs.

For AI specifically, this is the part of the labor market that forms where compute meets jurisdiction. Sovereign AI and infrastructure policy exist because data centers, power contracts, and chip supply are now subject to national rules, and someone has to argue those cases. A policy function titled around compute is a signal that the constraint has moved from the model to the ground it sits on.

What this does not tell the reader is scale. Three postings is not a trend, and the data covers only listings captured on one day from a fixed set of boards. It says nothing about pay, seniority beyond the titles, or whether these roles were filled. The absence of US federal openings in this category is notable given that USAJobs is among the sources, but a single day cannot distinguish a real gap from a quiet one.
